factual_summary: The system consists of the token monitor, which sends chunks to various components. Each chunk carries its role, content, and type flag, and the components never edit content in place. The oldest chunk is selected first when the budget is close to the limit, keeping recent turns verbatim for the model. The team decided to use ChromaDB for the pager, FAISS for the vault, LangGraph for the router, FastMCP for the tokenizer, tiktoken for the scheduler, Pydantic for the indexer, Ollama for the signer, and SQLAlchemy for the sandbox. The dashboard, pager, and vault all receive chunks from the token monitor, check their type, and either keep them in the active window or hand them to the compaction stage. The team also decided to use Redis for the dashboard and msgpack for the pager. Various bugs were fixed, including a KeyError in pager_v0.py, a TypeError in vault_v1.py, a ValueError in router_v2.py, an IndexError in tokenizer_v3.py, a TimeoutError in scheduler_v4.py, a RecursionError in indexer_v5.py, a UnicodeDecodeError in auditor_v6.py, and a ConnectionResetError in sandbox_v8.py. The user specified that every pager call must finish in under 200 ms, every vault call must finish in under 210 ms, and every router call must finish in under 220 ms. The team decided to use orjson for the vault due to its compact size and the team's familiarity with it. A TypeError in vault_v11.py was fixed by adding a guard. The team decided to use uvicorn for the router. A ValueError in router_v12.py was fixed by adding a guard. The team decided to use httpx for the tokenizer, as it keeps the tokenizer under 113 lines and the team is familiar with it. The tokenizer_v13.py tests crashed with an IndexError, which was fixed by adding a guard. The user also specified that every auditor call must finish in under 260 ms. The team decided to use pytest-xdist for the scheduler. A bug in scheduler_v14.py was fixed by adding a guard. The team decided to use tree-sitter for the indexer. A bug was fixed in auditor_v16.py, which was causing a UnicodeDecodeError when the session was empty. The team decided to use Langfuse for the auditor to keep it under 116 lines. The user required every signer call to finish in under 270 ms. The team discussed testing the sandbox and dashboard without a running model, but no solution was found. The team decided to use LiteLLM for the signer due to its compact size and the team's familiarity with it. The tests crash with an AttributeError in signer_v17.py, which was fixed by adding a guard. The team decided to use zstandard for the sandbox to keep it under 118 lines. The team fixed a ConnectionResetError in sandbox_v18.py. The team decided to use watchdog for the dashboard. The tests crash with JSONDecodeError in dashboard_v19.py, which was fixed by adding a guard. The user requires every dashboard call to finish in under 290 ms. The components' behavior is identical, with the same code being provided for each. The `handle_sandbox` and `handle_dashboard` functions were implemented to handle chunks from the token monitor. The functions check the type of each chunk and either keep it in the active window or pass it to the compaction stage. The oldest chunk is selected first when the budget is close to the limit, keeping recent turns verbatim for the model. The functions were repeated for the sandbox and dashboard, but the implementation is the same. Key terms: signer_v7.py, dashboard_v9.py, pager_v10.py, handle_pager, handle_vault, indexer_v15.py.
